packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 06 - FIRST READING (unverified image reading)

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this text. This is a blind reading. Beyond the stated rules: I listed the packet directory (filenames only) to find the images, and I cropped and rotated one region of image-006 and one of image-007 into my own scratch directory so I could read an upside-down note. No other directory, packet.json, web or search tool was used. All 26 images loaded.

Images: image-001 = overview of face 1 (shelf label in pencil at bottom margin: "Stams, StA, Fag. 240r"); image-002..013 = tiles of face 1 (3 columns x 4 rows). image-014 = overview of face 2 (label "Stams, StA, Fag. 240v"); image-015..026 = tiles of face 2 (3 x 4). Tiles overlap; overlapping lines are counted once below.

======================================================================
FACE 1 (image-001; tiles 002-013) - LAYOUT SURVEY
======================================================================
- Single parchment leaf, mounted on a modern support (grey Japanese-tissue repairs at top, left and bottom). Fold lines: one horizontal fold at about 1/3 height, vertical folds near left and right, forming panels (consistent with a document folded into a packet).
- No main text block is legible on this face. The upper panel (tiles 002-004, 006 top) shows only very faint grey traces of writing, probably show-through or offset from the other face; nothing is readable.
- Centre panel (tiles 005/006/008/009): a short dorsal note written UPSIDE DOWN relative to the image, in brown ink, with a later dark-ink shelf/number mark "104" (with a struck-through letter above, rotated 90 degrees) to its left. At the right (tile 007 lower, 010 top) a small block of 2-3 abraded lines written at 90 degrees; illegible.
- Many small worm/insect holes along the fold lines.

Reading of the upside-down note (image-006, lower part, read after 180-degree rotation; line 1 of the note):
  006 note-L1: [.]chatio[n]is? d(e)? bar[...]   (third word could be "bar" + 1-2 minims; final letters lost in abrasion)
  Alternative: first word could begin "s" or "e"; I can see "-chatio" or "-charo-" clearly, the rest is uncertain.
  008 (top right): "104" in later dark ink, preceded/surmounted by a cancelled letter or numeral (struck through).
  007/010: rotated 2-3 line block: [illegible] (abraded; only isolated letters visible).

Face 1 limitation: essentially an exterior/dorse face; no continuous text. A raking-light or UV image of the upper panel and of the rotated block at right might recover more.

======================================================================
FACE 2 (image-014; tiles 015-026) - LAYOUT SURVEY
======================================================================
- Single column of documentary Latin in a 16th-century humanist cursive / chancery hand, long lines (about 14-16 words), no ruling visible. Top edge torn diagonally (first 2 lines incomplete at left), bottom edge torn (last 2 lines incomplete), loss at right near the lower third (patched hole) and a patched hole mid-right.
- Three sections, visibly distinguished:
  (A) Top block, dark brown ink, ends with a subscription and date ("Die. 4. febrij 1514") and a publication clause; the word "CHRISTI" in large spaced display capitals mid-line (line 6), with following "nomine repetito" in lighter faded ink.
  (B) Middle block in lighter, more orange-brown ink (a different hand or pen), with a centred dating line "Die xiij februarij 1514." and a new paragraph beginning with an enlarged letter (Ill- / "Ill(ustri)s") with superscript "ris".
  (C) Lower block in dark brown ink again, opening "IN Christi nomine amen" with a large calligraphic I in the left margin (penwork flourishes, cadel-style strokes running down the margin from about line 26 to line 37 of the overview); "CHRisti" again in mixed display letters within the text; a faded display word "Cavalaritium?" (faded grey, like the "CHRISTI" in A).
- No glosses, no running titles. Abbreviations very heavy: s(e)n(ten)tia written "sntia", p(ro)/p(re)/p(er) by p with strokes, q(uondam) as "q.", Ill(ustrissi)mi as "Jllmi".
- Interpretation (tentative): a series of judicial acts (sentence on appeal, a delegation/commission, and a further sentence) with notarial publication clauses. I do not infer anything further.

Selected spans: all of A, B and C, i.e. essentially the whole face. Line numbering below is by physical line of the face as seen in overview image-014 (L1 = first surviving line at top); each line is given with the tiles in which it appears. Line breaks of the original are preserved; "|" marks where I join text across overlapping tiles. Hyphen at line end = hyphen in MS.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION A (tiles 015, 016, 017, 018, 019, 020)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
L1  (016 l.1 | 017 l.1): [torn] ...scriptis .D. pottati martinengi pro cit[...] [torn]
L2  (016 l.2 | 017 l.2): [torn] ...p(ro)cessus? sub sigillo formati in p(r)incipali causa in terra martinegi [torn]
     (first visible word "pcessus"/"pessus", initial letters lost at tear)
L3  (015 l.1 | 016 l.3 | 017 l.3): ...to comminatis. Et viso p(ro)cessu formato in ca(usa) p(rese)ntis app(ellati)onis, cu(m) o(mn)ibus et singulis acti[s?] [torn]
     (015 shows "to comminatis" — first letters lost at tear; word could be "...to cominatis" / "co(n)minatis")
L4  (015 l.2 | 016 l.4 | 017 l.4): [torn] ...p(ar)tis? et p(ro)ductis in dicta ca(usa) ad instantiam utriusq(ue) p(ar)tis. Visis dictis duob(us) testis. Et viso toto p(ro)cessu ta(m) p(r)incipalis
L5  (015 l.3 | 016 l.5 | 017 l.5): cau(s)e q(uam) app(ellati)onis. Et auditis nu(n)c et per antea p(ar)tes et p(ar)tes? dictis p(ar)tib(us) cu(m) eorum Advocatis et p(ro)curatorib(us) [underlined "bus"] in longa disputatione
     ("ptes et ptes" — two identical abbreviations; read as written)
L6  (015 l.4 | 016 l.6 | 017 l.6): et contradict(i)o(n)io? iudicio. Et co(n)sideratis? [word: "ẜhito"/"mhito"?] co(n)siderandis. Visa demu(m) citacione seu admonicione facta pro p(rese)nti die et hora ad
     ("cotradict" with superscript "io" — read "contradictorio"; word before "cosiderandis" uncertain, looks "mhito"/"inhito")
L7  (015 l.5 | 016 l.7 | 017 l.7): hanc n(ost)ram s(e)n(ten)tiam audienda(m) CHRISTI [display capitals] nomine repetito [faint ink] dicimus pronunciamus et s(e)n(ten)tiam(us) in hu(n)c modu(m) et formam v(idelicet)
L8  (015 l.6 | 016 l.8 | 017 l.8): Quia per hanc n(ost)ram s(e)n(ten)tiam diffinitiva(m) dicim(us) p(ro)nunciam(us) et s(e)n(ten)tiam(us) b(e)n(e) fuisse et esse iudicatu(m) per p(re)fatu(m)? [p with superscript "tu"] D. tu(n)c pottatem et p(ro)uiso-
L9  (015 l.7 | 016 l.9 | 017 l.9): rem martinegi in favore ssri? [abbrev. "ſſri"] Joannini de barberijs Inter(essa)tis? ["Jnter" + sup. "is"] tu(n)c ut s(upra): Et male Appellatu(m) per ssram? D. Antonia(m) ux(orem) [ox with sup. "om"?] ssri q(uondam) Antonij
     (the word before "D. Antonia" written "ſſtam"/"ſſram"; the same sign "ſſri" recurs; I leave it unexpanded)
L10 (015 l.8 | 016 l.10 | 017 l.10): de casarijs. Et consequenter dicta(m) s(e)n(ten)tiam ipsius .D. pottatis & p(ro)uisoris laudamus et co(n)firmamus: quia no(n) est p(ro)batu(m) legit(im)e
L11 (015 l.9 | 016 l.11 | 017 l.11): q(uod) testes fuerint rogati tempore co(n)fectionis dicti testam(en)ti ssri q(uondam) atonij [= Antonij] de casarijs, ut ex lectura processus co(n)stat. Ip(s)as? salvis
     ("Jp" + flourish before "salvis" — could be "Ipsis" or "Item"; uncertain)
L12 (015 l.10 | 016 l.12 | 017 l.12; also 018 l.2): p(re)missis partes ab expensis absol[v]imus [the "absol" retraced in darker ink] & liberamus propt(er) iusta(m) cau(s)am litiga(n)di. Et hec omnia omni meliori modo et c(etera)
L13 (015 l.11 | 016 l.13 | 017 l.13; 018 l.3): Et ita ut sup(ra) Dico et s(e)n(ten)tio Ego hier(onym)mus [sup. "mus"] de pischerijs Doct(or) ac Vicarius Ill(ustrissi)mi .D. Gubernat(or)is: et in hac p(ar)te a sua Ill(ustrissi)ma D(omi)natione De-
     (surname read "pischerijs"/"piscerijs"; the 3rd letter group is "sch" or "sc")
L14 (018 l.4 | 019 l.4 | 020 l.4): legat(us): In fide p(re)missor(um) me subscripsi ac sigillavi Die. 4. febrij. 1514. hora terciar(um) et iur(idi)ca et c(etera): Sigillat(a) sigillo p(ro)prio offi(ci)j p(re)fati
L15 (018 l.5 | 019 l.5 | 020 l.5): .D. Vicarij et Delegati ut s(upra). Lata lecta [underlined, written "Lata ſcta"] et publicata fuit suprascripta s(e)n(ten)tia: et ita dictu(m) & s(e)n(ten)tiatu(m) fuit per p(re)fatu(m)? [p + sup. "tu"] M(agnifi)c(u)m [M + sup. "cu"] et p(re)clar(um)
L16 (018 l.6 | 019 l.6 | 020 l.6): D. Hier(onym)m(u)m [sup. "mu"] de pischerijs Iur(is) utr(iusque) Doct(orem): Vicariu(m) et coram? [written "comar"/"coraz"?] Auditore(m) p(re)fati Ill(ustrissi)mi .D. Gubernat(or)is brix(ie), et in causa ssta? sp(eci)aliter
     ("et comar" before "Auditore" uncertain; may be "eius" + something; leave open)
L17 (018 l.8 | 019 l.8 | 020 l.8) [below the horizontal fold; ink becomes lighter]: Delegatu(m), sedente(m) pro iure reddendo ad eius solitu(m) iuris et offi(ci)j banchu(m) situ(m) in palacio novo communis brix(ie) in quo
L18 (018 l.9 | 019 l.9 | 020 l.9): pro communi brix(ie) iura redduntur contrate platee civitatis brix(ie): an(n)o a nativitat(e) D(omi)ni n(ost)ri Jesu Christi [xpi] millesimo quing(entesi)mo
L19 (018 l.10 | 019 l.10 | 020 l.10): quartodecimo Indictione secunda die quarto mensis febrij hora terciar(um) et iuridica: p(rese)ntibus Sp(ectabili) Doct(ore) .D. hier(onym)o [sup. "mo"] de
L20 (018 l.11 | 019 l.11 | 020 l.11): coffortis? [written "cofortis" with macron] et S(er) Hectore ganassono notario & alijs plurib(us) Testib(us) rogatis not(is) et vocat(is): In p(rese)ntia suprascriptor(um) Philippi
L21 (018 l.12 | 019 l.12 | 020 l.12): et Joa(n)nis marie fratru(m) filior(um) q(uondam) suprascripti Joannini de barberijs p(re)dicta acceptant(ium) in p(ar)tibus pro se tantummodo facient(ibus)
L22 (018 l.13 | 019 l.13 | 020 l.13): et in reliquis non consentient(ium) et c(etera): lecte et publicate [? "lecte"] me Lau[rentio?] [hole/stain, about 2 words: "...tes? dot..."?] not(ari)o? et Coadiutore [illegible ~1 word] Canc(ellar)ie? [sup. "ie"]
     (right half of this line is damaged by a hole and stain; "Coadiutor" fairly clear)
L23 (018 l.14 | 019 l.14 | 020 l.14): p(re)fati Ill(ustrissi)mi .D. Gubernator(is) brix(ie), de madato [= mandato] p(re)fati M(agnifi)ci .D. Audit(or)is et Delegati vi[...] [hole] qui de dicta s(e)n(ten)tia [hole] [..]ti? in o(mn)ibus
L24 (018 l.15 | 019 l.? ): ut supra, Laus Deo, —

----------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION B (tiles 019, 018/021, 022, 020/023) - lighter ink
----------------------------------------------------------------------
L25 (019 l.15 / 022 l.1) [centred]: Die xiij februarij. 1514.
L26 (021 l.3 | 022 l.2 | 023 l.3): Ill(ustri)s [enlarged "Ill" with sup. "ris" above] D(omi)n(u)s Gubernator brixie et bergomi existens in sala solite audientie palatij broletti brix(ie) [hole] [..]a? contradicto-
     (between "audientie" and "brolletti" a short word partly in a tear: "palatij"? — 023 shows "palatij broletti brix", reasonably clear)
L27 (021 l.4 | 022 l.3 | 023 l.4): rio iudicio Joa(n)ne petro de brianis? [hole] p(ro)c(urato)rio [sup. "io"] nomine intervenien(te) suprascripte .D. Antonie uxoris q(uondam) Antonij de casarijs et Bar-
     ("brianis"/"bzianis": the surname is uncertain; a hole follows it)
L28 (021 l.5 | 022 l.4 | 023 l.5): tholomeo de casarijs interveniente pro suo interesse ex una p(ar)te, et Joa(n)ne maria de barberijs interveniente pro se et Phi-
L29 (021 l.6 | 022 l.5 | 023 l.6): lippo eius fr(atr)e una cu(m) Fran(cis)co [sup. "co"] Lancino de bergomo ex altera, super causa s(e)n(ten)tie late per M(agnifi)c(u)m [sup. "u"] .D. Auditore(m) et dele-
L30 (021 l.7 | 022 l.6 | 023 l.7): gatu(m) in p(rese)nti processu: multisq(ue) per p(ar)tes dictis bene intellectis Comisit & delegavit hunc articulu(m) v(idelicet) an s(e)n(ten)tia p(re)fati
L31 (021 l.8 | 022 l.7 | 023 l.8): M(agnifi)ci .D. Auditoris sit co(n)formis s(e)n(ten)tie late per .D. potestatem tunc et p(ro)visore(m) martinegi vel ne: et consequenter an sit ap-
L32 (021 l.9 | 022 l.8 | 023 l.9): pellabilis vel no(n) appellabilis M(agnifi)co D(omi)no Pino de Numais? Equiti et Iur(is) utr(iusque) Doct(ori) et Iudici suo maleficior(um) ad Re-
     ("Numais"/"Numaiis": capital N, then "umais"; compare L39 "numaij")
L33 (021 l.10 | 022 l.9 | 023 l.10): ferendu(m) D(omi)nationi sue: presentibus Francisco padnano? [or "paduano"] et Joa(n)ne antonio de pro chartario testibus et c(etera) —

----------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION C (tiles 021, 022, 023, 024, 025, 026) - dark ink, large marginal initial I
----------------------------------------------------------------------
